result.title: Learning Where and How Much to Sample: Volume-Adaptive k-Space Acquisition for Accelerated MRI
result.summary: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential medical imaging technique, but its high costs and long acquisition times can limit accessibility. Accelerated MRI reduces acquisition time through k-space undersampling, yet conventional methods often rely on predefined sampling patterns and uniform slice budgets, overlooking anatomical variations and inter-slice relationships. In this paper, we propose a volume-adaptive k-space acquisition framework that jointly learns where and how much to sample across an entire MRI volume. Using only acquired auto-calibration signal (ACS) measurements, our method exploits volume-wide anatomical information to adaptively allocate sampling budgets across slices while identifying informative k-space lines. A learned joint slice--frequency refinement module coordinates sampling decisions while preserving an exact total volume-level acquisition budget. To reconstruct the acquired measurements, we design a sensitivity-aware synchronous cross-slice reconstruction network that estimates coil sensitivities from ACS measurements and progressively refines neighboring-slice reconstructions while enforcing hard k-space data consistency. Both networks are jointly optimized using reconstruction-based supervision without requiring fully sampled k-space at inference. Experiments on knee and brain MRI across multiple contrasts and acceleration factors demonstrate the adaptive behavior of our acquisition framework and evaluate its reconstruction performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出面向加速 MRI 的体数据自适应 k 空间采样框架，仅用已采集的 ACS 信号联合学习在每个 slice 上「采样哪里、采样多少」，在保持总体采集预算不变的前提下分配预算，并配套跨 slice 的灵敏度感知重建网络与硬数据一致性约束。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用廉价已有测量预测证据价值、在固定总预算下学习何处取多少」的机制，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的计算分配有形式上的类比，但领域相距较远，可供核查其预算约束与决策可解释性设计。
